cases.title: Absolute change filter: inclusive boundary in both directions, source-level default, channel override, per-channel state
cases.intent: An Absolute change filter passes a value when it is at or beyond lastPassed +/- Value (ChangeFilter.kt:30-33, 113-114, inclusive). Counters 0..20 and 100..120 under a source-level Abs5 must yield exactly 0,5,10,15,20 and 100,105,...,120 - one filter instance per channel (ChangeFiltersCache.kt:43-47), so the two do not interfere - and the wrap back to Min passes because the drop is >= 5. 'ovr' overrides the source filter with Abs20 at channel level (ChangeFiltersCache.kt:40) and yields 0,20. 'rng' steps by exactly +5 and -5 and by +4/-1: only the exact-5 steps pass, proving the boundary is inclusive both ways. A String channel passes once, then every change throws inside the filter, which is caught, logged and treated as 'filtered' (ChangeFiltersCache.kt:63-69).

assert.comment: 'A' passes once as the first value; 'B' throws, a returning 'A' equals the baseline

cases.title: Type=Always never moves its baseline, so a value that returns to the first one is suppressed forever (known defect); docs-spelled keys are ignored
cases.intent: For Type=Always a changed value returns true without updating lastPassedValue (ChangeFilter.kt:91-94), so the first value stays the baseline: A,B,A,B emits A,B,B,B and 1,2,1,2 emits 1,2,2,2 - the moment a signal returns to its starting value it disappears. The 'docs' channel uses the keys from the documentation example (docs/core/change-filter-configuration.md:94-95, FilterType/FilterValue); the code reads Type/Value (ChangeFilterConfiguration.kt:72-73) and silently defaults to Always (:24), so the 'Absolute 5' filter passes 1 right after 0. An unfiltered counter makes every read a record, so counts are counts of reads.

assert.comment: Absolute 5 would never pass 1 after 0: the docs keys were ignored and Always applied

knownDefect.summary: Type=Always passes a changed value without updating lastPassedValue, so every later occurrence of the first value is treated as unchanged and suppressed

cases.title: AtLeast re-sends an unchanged value; AtLeast 0 passes every repeat; AtLeast is never applied to in-window changes (known defect)
cases.intent: AtLeast is consulted only when the new value equals the last passed one (ChangeFilter.kt:75-87, compared with >= at :80). So a constant under AtLeast 0 passes on every read, a constant under AtLeast 500 is re-sent periodically - asserted only by loose read-count bounds, since it is time-based - and its value never changes. But a counter that moves by less than the threshold is never re-sent: 1..4 between 0 and 5 do not pass even though 200 ms elapse, which contradicts the documented guarantee that at least one value passes per AtLeast period 'regardless of whether the value has changed or met the filter value threshold' (docs/core/change-filter-configuration.md:20).

assert.comment: Time-based: about every 5th read at a 100 ms interval. Only wide bounds: it must repeat (min 2) and must not pass every read (max 20 of 30)

knownDefect.summary: AtLeast only re-sends identical values; a value that changes by less than the threshold is never passed, contrary to the documented minimum reporting interval

assertCorrect.comment: With a 200 ms AtLeast and 100 ms reads, some of the in-window values must pass

cases.title: Negative change-filter Value and AtLeast are accepted and silently disable filtering (known defect)
cases.intent: ChangeFilterConfiguration.validate() rejects a negative Value or AtLeast (ChangeFilterConfiguration.kt:36-61), but nothing calls it: ControllerServiceConfiguration only checks that the referenced ID exists (:258-276). A negative Value makes low > high, so every value passes; a negative AtLeast makes the period always expired, so a constant passes on every read. The configuration should be rejected at startup; today it runs and filters nothing.

knownDefect.summary: ChangeFilterConfiguration.validate() is never invoked, so Value -5 and AtLeast -1000 are accepted and disable the filter

cases.title: Percent change filter follows a geometric progression; on negative values it filters nothing (known defect)
cases.intent: A Percent filter's window is lastPassed +/- lastPassed*Value/100 (ChangeFilter.kt:35-38). A counter 10..160 step 10 under 50% must pass exactly 10,20,30,50,80,120 (each value at least 1.5x the last passed one, or after the wrap at most half of it); every intermediate step is filtered. For a negative last value the computed dif is negative, so low > high and the 'outside' predicate at :113-114 is true for every value: a 10% filter on a signal around -100 passes all of -100..-90 instead of only -100 and -90.

knownDefect.summary: The Percent window dif = last * Value/100 is not sign-safe: for a negative last value low > high and every value passes

cases.title: Condition filters present/absent/any/all/none/and/or over a 4-phase trigger pattern; operands are channel IDs, not names
cases.intent: Two triggers share one 4-phase counter: t1 passes its value filter in phases 2 and 3, t2 in phases 1 and 3, so the four phases realise all four presence combinations. Each constant channel carries one condition filter, evaluated against the source's post-value-filter channel map keyed by channel ID (ScheduleReader.kt:621-642, SourceReadResult.kt:36-37). The exact key set of every phase is asserted (selected by the unfiltered phase counter 'ph'), so a wrong operator or a filter evaluated on the wrong snapshot changes a set. 'wn' is conditioned on 'Trigger1', t1's output Name: filters see IDs, so it never passes - while the payload key of t1 IS its Name.

cases.title: only/notonly count the surviving channel map; a dotted JMESPath reaches into a Structure value
cases.intent: 'only' passes when the source's post-value-filter map holds exactly one channel, 'notonly' when it holds more (OnlyValueConditionFilter.kt:11-12, NotOnlyValueConditionFilter.kt:11-12). A 0/1 trigger behind eq 1 toggles the map size, so srcOnly alternates between {onlyCh} and {tA}, and srcNot between absent and {tB, notonlyCh}. A present condition with 'status.state' is a JMESPath into a Structure channel's value (FilterBuilder.kt:99-101) and passes; 'status.nosuch' does not. Assertions are per source, because the source order in a record follows completion order.

cases.title: Malformed value and condition filters are accepted and pass everything (known defect)
cases.intent: Validation only checks the top-level operator name (ControllerServiceConfiguration.kt:154-166, FilterConfiguration.kt:33-40). Everything else fails open: non-object elements of an and/or array are dropped (FilterConfigurationDeserializer.kt:47-58, FilterBuilder.kt:77-82) and a nested unknown operator builds to null and is dropped too (FilterBuilder.kt:94-97), leaving an empty And or Or, which passes every value (AndFilter.kt:16, OrFilter.kt:20). A condition filter with a numeric Value yields no expression (FilterBuilder.kt:99-108), create returns null (PresentConditionFilter.kt:32), the cache drops it (ConditionFiltersCache.kt:16-21) and a missing filter passes (ScheduleReader.kt:631). A typo in a filter therefore silently disables it.

knownDefect.summary: Malformed and/or groups, nested unknown operators and non-string condition values build to empty or missing filters, which pass everything instead of being rejected

cases.title: Stage order: transformation before value filter; condition filters see the post-change-filter map
cases.intent: processReceivedData applies transformations, then change and value filters, then condition filters (ScheduleReader.kt:331-334, 597-618). 'c' is multiplied by 10 and then filtered with gt 150: it passes for raw 16..20 as 160..200, which is only possible if the filter sees transformed values (raw values never exceed 20). 'd' is conditioned on 't' being present, and 't' sits behind an Absolute 5 change filter: 'd' appears exactly in the reads where 't' survived the change filter, so the condition filter evaluates the post-change-filter map. Over the shared 21-read cycle the records are phases 0,5,10,15 {t,d}, 16..19 {c} and 20 {c,t,d}.

cases.title: Every value-filter comparator (word and symbol forms), nested and/or groups and a single-object group
cases.intent: Ten lockstep counters 0..10, each behind one value filter. Within a read all counters hold the same value, and each filter's pass set over a full cycle is exact: gt/>, >=, lt, <=, ==, ne, an and-range [3,6], a nested '0 or (>=5 and !=8 and <11)' and an 'or' whose Value is a single object rather than an array (FilterConfigurationDeserializer.kt:61-63). Filter values are compared as doubles (FilterConfigurationDeserializer.kt:41, DataTypes.kt:66-73). Every read passes at least one channel (lt or ge), so records equal reads and a cycle missing from a channel is a filtering error, not a missing record.

cases.title: String and Boolean equality filters; eq with a JSON number never matches a numeric string (known defect)
cases.intent: EqualValueFilter compares a String channel with the filter value's toString() and a Boolean with a Boolean (EqualValueFilter.kt:21-26). An or-group of two string eq filters passes exactly ERROR and CRITICAL of a 4-value range; eq true passes a true constant and eq false blocks it; eq "5" passes the string "5". But a numeric filter value is deserialized as a Double (FilterConfigurationDeserializer.kt:41), so eq 5 compares "5" with "5.0" and never matches.

knownDefect.summary: Numeric filter values are Doubles and a String channel is compared with value.toString(), so eq 5 compares "5" with "5.0" and never matches
